From 0024430e920f2900654ad83cd081cf52e02a3ef5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nathan Chancellor <nathan@kernel.org>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2021 12:01:06 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] x86/build: Fix location of '-plugin-opt=' flags

Commit b33fff07e3e3 ("x86, build: allow LTO to be selected") added a
couple of '-plugin-opt=' flags to KBUILD_LDFLAGS because the code model
and stack alignment are not stored in LLVM bitcode.

However, these flags were added to KBUILD_LDFLAGS prior to the
emulation flag assignment, which uses ':=', so they were overwritten
and never added to $(LD) invocations.

The absence of these flags caused misalignment issues in the
AMDGPU driver when compiling with CONFIG_LTO_CLANG, resulting in
general protection faults.

Shuffle the assignment below the initial one so that the flags are
properly passed along and all of the linker flags stay together.

At the same time, avoid any future issues with clobbering flags by
changing the emulation flag assignment to '+=' since KBUILD_LDFLAGS is
already defined with ':=' in the main Makefile before being exported for
modification here as a result of commit:

  ce99d0bf312d ("kbuild: clear LDFLAGS in the top Makefile")

Fixes: b33fff07e3e3 ("x86, build: allow LTO to be selected")
Reported-by: Anthony Ruhier <aruhier@mailbox.org>
Signed-off-by: Nathan Chancellor <nathan@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>
Tested-by: Anthony Ruhier <aruhier@mailbox.org>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://github.com/ClangBuiltLinux/linux/issues/1374
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210518190106.60935-1-nathan@kernel.org

diff --git a/arch/x86/Makefile b/arch/x86/Makefile
index c77c5d8a7b3e..307529417021 100644
--- a/arch/x86/Makefile
+++ b/arch/x86/Makefile
@@ -178,11 +178,6 @@ ifeq ($(ACCUMULATE_OUTGOING_ARGS), 1)
 	KBUILD_CFLAGS += $(call cc-option,-maccumulate-outgoing-args,)
 endif
 
-ifdef CONFIG_LTO_CLANG
-KBUILD_LDFLAGS	+= -plugin-opt=-code-model=kernel \
-		   -plugin-opt=-stack-alignment=$(if $(CONFIG_X86_32),4,8)
-endif
-
 # Workaround for a gcc prelease that unfortunately was shipped in a suse release
 KBUILD_CFLAGS += -Wno-sign-compare
 #
@@ -202,7 +197,12 @@ ifdef CONFIG_RETPOLINE
   endif
 endif
 
-KBUILD_LDFLAGS := -m elf_$(UTS_MACHINE)
+KBUILD_LDFLAGS += -m elf_$(UTS_MACHINE)
+
+ifdef CONFIG_LTO_CLANG
+KBUILD_LDFLAGS	+= -plugin-opt=-code-model=kernel \
+		   -plugin-opt=-stack-alignment=$(if $(CONFIG_X86_32),4,8)
+endif
 
 ifdef CONFIG_X86_NEED_RELOCS
 LDFLAGS_vmlinux := --emit-relocs --discard-none
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `arch/x86/Makefile`**
1. The block of code that adds `-plugin-opt=` flags to `KBUILD_LDFLAGS` has been moved below the assignment of `KBUILD_LDFLAGS` to ensure that these flags are not overwritten.
2. The assignment of `KBUILD_LDFLAGS` has been changed from `:=` to `+=` to prevent future clobbering of flags, allowing for the accumulation of linker flags.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modifications are related in that they both address the issue of ensuring that the `-plugin-opt=` flags are correctly included in the linker flags used during the build process. By moving the assignment of these flags below the main `KBUILD_LDFLAGS` assignment and changing the assignment operator, the patch ensures that the flags are preserved and properly passed along in the build process, thus preventing misalignment issues in the AMDGPU driver when using LTO with Clang.

The `+=` operator for the `-plugin-opt=` flags is placed before the `KBUILD_LDFLAGS` initialization, causing these flags to be overwritten and not included in the final linker invocation.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```makefile
KBUILD_LDFLAGS += -m elf_$(UTS_MACHINE)
ifdef CONFIG_LTO_CLANG
KBUILD_LDFLAGS	+= -plugin-opt=-code-model=kernel \
```
Reason:
Changing `KBUILD_LDFLAGS :=` to `KBUILD_LDFLAGS +=` allows the initial value to be appended rather than overwritten. This ensures that the `-plugin-opt=` flags are correctly included in the linker flags, preventing the misalignment issues in the AMDGPU driver when compiling with `CONFIG_LTO_CLANG`.
